items.text: Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the Nov 3 midterms, according to network projections. CBS projects at least 54 Democratic Senate seats. Reported Senate flips include Texas (Talarico over Paxton), Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina. House races were still being counted.
items.notes: Results are projections, and outlets' House totals differ (CBS projects 251–268 Democratic seats). The defeated South Carolina Republican's name appears garbled in some outlets, so it is left out. CNBC pages would not load.

items.text: The Mississippi and Alaska Senate races were still too close to call on Nov 5. In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Hyde-Smith by about 1,100 votes with 96% counted. In Alaska, Mary Peltola led Sen. Sullivan by about 640 votes, with ranked-choice tabulation still to come.
items.notes: Mississippi has no formal recount process, so a legal fight is possible.

items.text: Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek the post of House Republican leader in the next Congress. Scalise and Jordan are reported to be running, and the vote is reportedly set for Nov 10. Jeffries has launched his bid for Speaker, and Schumer says he will be majority leader.

Vice President Vance wrote that Republicans lost because of the Iran war. Trump called that largely true because of gasoline prices, but said he would go to war again, and also blamed weak candidates.
items.notes: Framing differs. Fox describes Republicans as soul-searching, citing Cruz on prices, tariffs and the war. NBC and the Washington Post frame the result as a rejection of Trump. The Washington Post is paywalled.

items.text: The lame-duck Congress returns on Nov 9 facing a Dec 11 government-funding deadline. Also pending are the NDAA, a possible debt-limit increase and HHS confirmations, which Republicans want done before they lose the Senate on Jan 3.

The US and Iran remain far apart. Qatar is seeking backing for a draft that starts with three days of confidence-building steps, while Iran wants the blockade and sanctions lifted before it reopens Hormuz. Axios reports a US strike on Qeshm Island on Nov 3, and Trump says he is in 'no rush' to resume strikes.
Iran's IRGC said two tankers and a tug caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, one after hitting a mine, after they used 'unauthorised' routes. This has not been independently verified.
The Dow jumped about 1,570 points on Nov 4 and Brent fell about 8%, to the mid-$90s. On Nov 5 chip stocks sold off (AMD −13%, Nvidia −7%) on fears of tougher AI rules under a Democratic Congress.
items.notes: Intraday figures; index levels differed between sources.

items.text: Challenger counted 43,994 announced US job cuts in October, slightly more than September but 71% fewer than a year earlier.
Voters in Washington and Arizona approved measures restricting transgender athletes in girls' sports, with about 56% and 58%, Fox reports. Roughly 160 statewide measures were on ballots nationwide.

The FDA announced several recalls. Evergreen Fresh broccoli sprouts are linked to a Salmonella outbreak (34 ill in six states; CDC says it is over), Once Upon a Farm toddler bars pose a choking risk, and Brad's kale chips may contain thallium.
The Supreme Court's November sitting continued with argument in Guerrero v. Johnson (25-1003).

The CDC's Ebola attestation order took effect at 11:59pm EST on Nov 3. Every international air passenger must attest they have not been in DR Congo in the past 21 days, and separate entry suspensions for DRC, Uganda and South Sudan run to Nov 10.

The RPP held the reference rate at 3.75%. The new NBP projection puts 2027 CPI at 3.1–5.3%, assuming fuel price caps end on Dec 31. At his Nov 5 press conference Glapiński said no hike has been decided and that inflation would be much lower if the caps were extended.
items.outlet: TVN24 Biznes; PAP via Portal Samorządowy

items.text: The Constitutional Tribunal dispute escalated. A judges' assembly chaired by Anna Korwin-Piotrowska ruled that 8 of 12 judges is enough to pass resolutions and called another assembly for Nov 10. Święczkowski and Sochański, who say they are the lawful leadership, called this an unlawful attack.
items.notes: Coverage splits. TVN24 and RMF present the assembly as restoring the Tribunal's work. wPolityce calls Korwin-Piotrowska a 'usurper' (headline only read: https://wpolityce.pl/polityka/juz-wyglasza-oredzia-uzurpatorka-nadaje-z-fotela-prezesa-tk,290312). Euronews notes expert criticism of the quorum ruling.

items.text: After a four-hour National Security Council meeting on Nov 3, Tusk offered President Nawrocki a one-on-one meeting, and Nawrocki agreed. The presidential spokesman says it will be soon but may not be this week. Nawrocki blamed Tusk for a 'serious constitutional crisis'.
items.reporter: Arleta Zalewska, Konrad Piasecki; Maria Literacka

items.text: Tusk countersigned the president's appointment of four new NBP board members, including Ludwik Kotecki and Przemysław Litwiniuk, so the board does not fall below its legal minimum. Money.pl reports the Sejm vote on putting Glapiński before the State Tribunal has slipped to January.
items.notes: The money.pl piece is opinion. The names of the other two appointees were not fully confirmed. Nawrocki's final signature was pending.

items.text: Because of constitutional doubts over the Senate's amendments, the government resubmitted its PIT/CIT reform as a new bill, which passed first reading on Nov 5. It keeps a 130k zł PIT threshold with a new 24% band, a 5% solidarity levy and 22% CIT for firms with revenue above €50m.

The Senate health committee rejected PiS's motion to throw out the bill restoring abortion for severe foetal defects, which requires the procedure within 72 hours of consent. The full Senate votes on Nov 6.
Tusk named KO deputy mayor Łukasz Pabiś as commissioner for Częstochowa, whose mayor and council were recalled by referendum. An early election must be held within 90 days.
Tusk says he has signed and sent the papers appointing Agnieszka Bartol as funds minister and Andrzej Domański as deputy prime minister, and expects Nawrocki to sign quickly.

Hackers remotely took over refrigeration controllers at three Auchan stores, a small grocery and a food distributor. CERT Polska found 140 exposed devices, and Digital Affairs Minister Gawkowski warned firms to disconnect them or be publicly named. Pro-Kremlin groups claimed some attacks, but this is unverified.
items.notes: The attacks ran from late October, with a new wave overnight on Nov 1–2. GIS advised regular checks with independent thermometers. They are part of a wider wave in France, Belgium, Sweden and Luxembourg.

items.text: Mayor Gibała signed an order cutting the residents' monthly network pass from 99 zł to 90 zł, but only from Sep 1, 2027. A separate fare overhaul planned for Jan 4, 2027 (a 4 zł 20-minute ticket, and the 30-minute ticket extended to 40 minutes) still awaits its second reading.

Gibała will ask the city council to take Kraków out of several organisations, including Eurocities and the Healthy Cities association, to save about 8.2m zł a year. He also abolished the post held by Aleksandra Twaróg.
items.thread: Gibała's first months as Kraków mayor
items.notes: This is the only new concrete saving towards the roughly 390m zł spending gap (watch W-261027-09).

items.text: Despite residents' protests, UKEN began building its shooting range at Fort Bronowice under a voivode's permit, and park access is restricted from Nov 4. Residents have announced an appeal.
The Border Guard stopped a 38-year-old Ukrainian in central Kraków who was listed in Schengen databases as an undesirable person. He was ordered to leave Poland and given a 10-month entry ban.
Kraków prosecutors say the most likely explanation of July's four deaths in Skawina is that the man killed the others and then himself. Toxicology found no alcohol or drugs.

On Nov 4 the Union Cabinet approved Rs 14,500 crore of viability-gap funding for 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage, with 40% domestic content required for battery projects. It also approved Rs 2,814 crore for lithium and nickel processing and a Rs 4,371 crore statistics programme that includes the 8th Economic Census.
items.notes: The PIB release was not opened directly; figures come via Vajiram & Ravi's summary of it.

items.text: The Cabinet extended the fast-track special courts scheme for rape and POCSO cases to March 2031 with Rs 3,788 crore, raising the number of courts from 779 to 850.

The Supreme Court issued notice on RJD MP Manoj Jha's challenge to the lifelong legal immunity given to election commissioners under the CEC Act 2023. CJI Surya Kant asked that no further similar petitions be filed.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: The main pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar were deferred and are likely around Nov 17.

items.text: At a Congress protest in Bengaluru, Siddaramaiah demanded that SIR be scrapped and that the CEC resign. He claimed Karnataka's rolls fell by more than 99 lakh voters. No response from the ECI or BJP was reported.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR

items.text: Amit Shah and Nirmala Sitharaman challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate SIR and 'vote chori' in a special Parliament session. Congress continues to press for paper ballots. No session has been announced.
items.thread: Opposition vs Election Commission over SIR
items.notes: Coverage splits. Asianet/ANI carried the opposition's crowd claims for the Nov 1 rally and BJP's 'PR exercise' line. Swarajya puts 'vote chori' in scare quotes, while Siasat/PTI led with Kharge's charges.

items.text: Amar Ujala reports that the CDS has announced a two-year extension for Agniveers completing their four-year term; the first batch exits on Nov 21. No PIB notification or English wire confirmation has been found.
items.notes: A Nov 2 report said only that the Defence Ministry had a draft awaiting Cabinet approval.

items.text: India launched three indigenous AI models (EKA-1, Dhir 2B and Dhir 5B) that work in Indian languages, some of them offline. Amar Ujala separately reports a Home Ministry alert about AI agents attacking banks.
items.notes: The Home Ministry alert is single-source.

items.text: At the Navy's Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue (Nov 3–5), Rajnath Singh said undersea cables and maritime infrastructure must be protected, not just sea lanes.
The Supreme Court asked the Centre to set up a special cell to monitor enforcement of the child labour law.
The Karnataka High Court quashed the BJP's defamation case against Siddaramaiah over the 'corruption rate card' ads.
Delhi's air quality worsened, with stubble smoke the main cause. The Supreme Court allows certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR only on Nov 7–8, with the full ban back from Nov 9.

PiS's Mariusz Błaszczak told RMF FM that the projected Democratic win means a permanent US base in Poland will not be built, and blamed the Tusk government. The government had not responded, and Kosiniak-Kamysz still expects a White House decision on the base in December.
items.notes: This is an opposition politician's assessment, not a US decision. The Kosiniak-Kamysz–Hegseth meeting is still expected 'after the midterms'.

items.text: PTI, citing unnamed sources, says the midterm results will not affect the interim India–US trade deal because it needs no Congressional approval. Analysts disagree: GTRI says a weakened Trump may close the deal within about two months, while Emkay says the urgency has eased. Indian goods still face a 10% Section 301 duty.
items.outlet: PTI via Siasat; The Tribune / ANI

items.text: Diplomatic sources say Modi and Trump may meet on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila (about Nov 16–18), with trade, tariffs and visas on the agenda.
items.notes: Trump's attendance in Manila is confirmed separately (The Star); the bilateral meeting is not.

items.text: IT ministry sources say CERT-In now has access to Anthropic's restricted Mythos model under Project Glasswing, to look for weaknesses in critical systems. Officials plan a slow rollout because the model is cloud-only. (This desk is produced with Anthropic's Claude.)
The fifth India–US tri-service disaster-relief exercise, Tiger Triumph, opened in Visakhapatnam, with India's National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) taking part for the first time.

Indian Minister of State for Commerce Jitin Prasada led a 12-company delegation to Warsaw. He discussed AI, semiconductors, data centres and critical minerals with Deputy PM Gawkowski and visited WB Electronics. No agreements were signed.
